newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end down in thin, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end down in thin, slow trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Monday as the market succumbed to concerns about the potential fallout from Nomura Securities' disclosure last week that two of its directors had been involved in suspected illegal deals.

Dealers said trading volumes were thin and activity slow due to a lack of fresh factors and the market's failure to find inspiration in the Dow's firm close on Friday after the release of tame U.S. employment data.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract lost 125 points to close at 18,055 on volume of 15,570 lots.
"Everybody thinks the BOJ (Bank of Japan) can't raise rates anyway, so the U.S. market is having very little effect on the Japanese market," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
He said the March Nikkei looked set for a technical rebound to 18,200-18,300. "I would just sell on any rebound. I'm not willing to go on the long side," he added.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 345.7 against its opening 346.5 on volume of 93 lots.
